record.title: One appearance table for every picture
record.choice: Derive how a node and a relation are drawn - tone, shape, outline and line - from one table keyed on the rendering contract's closed enums, and read that table from both the map and the generated diagram; a renderer adds only its own pixels.
alternatives: Style the map in its stylesheet and leave the generated diagram as one flat rectangle per node.
Ship the palette as a consumer-facing asset beside the UI copy.
record.because: A second palette drifts, so the same zone or interaction kind would read differently in the map than in the generated documentation, and a value the contract allows could reach a renderer with no display token at all.
consequences: A value added to a contract enum fails the appearance suite until it is given a token.
Tones belong to the shared vocabulary while dash lengths, stroke widths and radii stay with the surface that draws them.

records.title: Archivarius
records.purpose: One validated JSON file - a snapshot - holds a project's whole description as small linked records: its parts, the rules they must satisfy, the decisions behind them, the work left and the checks that confirm it. A React library draws that file as an architecture map that reveals more detail as it is zoomed.

records.title: Purpose of the library
records.statement: An owner understands a system's structure, the grounds for decisions, the remaining work and the effect of changes from one snapshot; an LLM reads and edits the same records.

records.title: The repository describes itself
records.statement: The snapshot in this repository describes Archivarius itself, so the map below, the tables under it and this page are the project's own records drawn by the library it documents.

records.title: Provenance and freshness model
records.statement: A record keeps the definitions it was written against apart from the records it merely mentions, so when a definition changes, whatever rested on it stops counting as confirmed instead of quietly staying green.

records.title: Model and contract
records.summary: Owns the v4 JSON schema, record types, graph references, history, snapshots and the validated-change contract.

records.title: Core
records.summary: Parses and validates a model, projects a v4 project to an architecture, and analyzes freshness and completion.
records.boundary: Layout and rendering stay outside the core.

records.title: Graph references
records.summary: Validates typed relations between records and reports reverse links and coverage.
records.boundary: Reference semantics are fixed by the schema targets.

records.title: Canonical digest
records.summary: Computes the SHA-256 basis over a canonical representation of the definitions.
records.boundary: The canonicalization rules are internal to the digest.

records.title: Node API
records.summary: Reads a model file, verifies evidence artifacts by bytes, applies validated changes, and generates documentation.

records.boundary: Project data and UI copy stay external resources.

records.title: Model source
records.payload: A v4 JSON snapshot as a URL, File, Blob or parsed object.
records.meaning: Any accepted source resolves to one parsed snapshot before anything renders, and a snapshot that fails validation is never partly displayed.

records.title: Change input
records.payload: A context receipt and a change with put and remove sets.
records.meaning: The receipt fixes the definitions the change was written against, so a change computed from definitions that have since moved cannot land.

records.title: Evidence artifact
records.payload: Relative binding paths and the bytes they resolve to.
records.meaning: A declared path confirms only while its bytes still match, so an artifact that was moved or edited stops confirming on the next read.

records.title: Reference set
records.meaning: Every relation resolves to an existing record of a type its field allows, and whatever nothing points at is reported as uncovered.

records.title: Basis value
records.payload: The canonical definitions and their SHA-256 basis.
records.meaning: Equal definitions yield an equal basis whatever their order or edit history, so a differing basis means a definition really changed.

records.title: Record detail
records.payload: A selected record with its links and implementation outcome.
records.meaning: A record arrives with its links and outcome already resolved, so what is shown never depends on a second read of the model.

records.title: Views agree with the snapshot
records.assertion: The map, inspector and generated documentation all reflect the same loaded snapshot and definitions.

records.assertion: A stale context, unknown field or broken reference is rejected and the input model is left unmodified.

records.title: Confirmation needs byte-exact evidence
records.rule: A check outcome confirms only with an available execution artifact and matching bytes for every declared input; missing or stale evidence does not confirm.
when: An implementation outcome is derived.

records.title: Stale and missing evidence cannot confirm
records.assertion: A result confirms only when its artifact exists and every declared input's bytes match; otherwise the criterion is not confirmed.

records.title: Conservative freshness
records.rule: Changing any definition conservatively marks dependent decisions, tasks and checks as requiring review; the current review scope is the whole project.
when: A definition changes.

records.title: Dependents are marked for review
records.assertion: After a definition changes, decisions, tasks and checks depending on it report their basis as no longer current.

records.title: Canonical digest for the basis
records.choice: Compute basis.contract as a SHA-256 over a canonical representation of the definitions, excluding results, history and review text.
alternatives: Track freshness by timestamps or manual review flags.
records.because: A content digest detects real definition changes without trusting order or edit metadata.
consequences: Any definition change, including additions, drops the current basis.

records.title: Project data and copy stay external
records.choice: Load model data and UI copy as external resources rather than bundling them into the library.
alternatives: Embed a default model and copy in the shipped scripts.
records.because: The format stays independent of any project, repository or build, and shipped scripts do not carry project data.
consequences: A consumer supplies the model source and container.

steps: Read a focused record's context.

records.title: A claim can be aged and questioned
records.rule: Every record states when it was last changed and by whom or what, so a claim can be aged, attributed and questioned.

records.title: Expansion follows the threshold
records.assertion: A container expands into its children when its box crosses the threshold and collapses back with hysteresis, and the map states which level is shown.

records.title: A link restores the view
records.assertion: Opening a shared link restores the focus, the expanded containers and the open panel, and the map exports the current view as a vector and a raster image.

records.title: No action needs a pointer
records.assertion: Every control and every part is reachable and operable by keyboard, the map is one tab stop with traversal inside it, and closing a panel returns focus to its opener.

records.title: Untyped changes reach assistive technology
records.assertion: A zoom, expansion, focus, panel or failure change is published to a live region naming the new state.

records.title: Reader settings survive the map
records.assertion: With reduced motion, forced colours, a dark scheme or doubled text size the map stays usable, and every zone, kind and relation kind reads without colour.

records.title: Every code is documented and typed
records.assertion: Every code the library can throw appears in the shipped code table and in the declared code union, and no undocumented code is reachable.

records.title: A consumer mounts from the docs
records.assertion: The shipped documentation carries install, mount, stylesheet, asset-path and validation instructions that run as written.

records.title: A release states what it promises
records.assertion: The package ships a license and a changelog entry per version and states the contract versions it accepts.

records.title: A stated size stays interactive
records.assertion: At the stated node count layout runs off the interface thread, only visible parts are mounted, and first paint and interaction stay inside the budget.

records.title: A bound is reported, not hit silently
records.assertion: An input over the size limit, a layout over the timeout and an aborted read each fail with their own code and leave no work running.

records.title: Authoring starts and fails helpfully
records.assertion: A generated skeleton validates, every record type has a template, a rehearsed change writes nothing, and every diagnostic names the field and the fix.

records.title: A binding narrows to what it claims
records.assertion: A record binds several files and a range within a file, and an edit outside every bound range leaves the confirmation standing.

records.title: Withdrawal is proportionate
records.assertion: A definition change withdraws only dependent records, and a subtree review restores currency without touching unrelated records.

records.title: A comparison names what moved
records.assertion: Comparing two snapshots reports each added, removed, re-parented, re-zoned and re-confirmed record, and the map can show the difference.

records.title: Declared and actual edges are reconciled
records.assertion: Verification reports every declared relation the code no longer has and every dependency the code has that no record declares.

records.title: A record carries its age and author
records.assertion: Every record states its last change time and author, and both survive a round trip through apply and archive.

records.title: Only a run can pass a check
records.assertion: A check without a command is refused, and an outcome written without a matching execution artifact does not confirm.

records.title: Content cannot act
records.assertion: Model content renders as text with no executable markup or active link, and no request leaves the surface beyond the declared model and asset reads.

records.title: The import graph stays a directed layer table
records.assertion: The import graph is acyclic and points down the layer table, and no module outside the loader reads a file or the network.

records.title: Regeneration is a no-op
records.assertion: Regenerating every shipped document leaves the bytes unchanged, and a hand edit is reported as drift.

records.title: One language ships
records.assertion: The shipped copy declares English, no exported function takes a locale, and the mounted subtree states its language.

records.title: A snapshot renders outside the map
records.assertion: A standalone diagram, a self-contained page and an image are generated from the projection and open without the library.

records.title: Search moves the map
records.assertion: Searching from the map finds a part by name and moves the view to it, and a filter removes out-of-scope parts from the canvas.

records.title: Reach is answered on the map
records.assertion: The map reports the path between two parts, the transitive dependents of a part and any cycle among them.

records.title: Detail as a function of interest
records.statement: Furnas, Generalized Fisheye Views, CHI 1986 (https://doi.org/10.1145/22627.22342): a display that holds full detail near the point of interest and degrades it with distance shows a structure larger than the screen, so how much detail a part gets is a function of interest rather than a separate view the reader has to open.

records.title: One zoomable surface with representations that change
records.statement: Perlin and Fox, Pad, SIGGRAPH 1993 (https://doi.org/10.1145/166117.166125), and Bederson and Hollan, Pad++, UIST 1994 (https://doi.org/10.1145/192426.192435): on one continuous zoomable surface an object may change its representation at a size threshold - semantic zoom - which replaces a stack of separate diagrams with a single space.

records.title: Zooming alone loses the context it hides
records.statement: Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson, A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, ACM Computing Surveys 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1145/1456650.1456652): pure zooming costs the reader the surrounding context and the memory of where they were, so a zoomable map owes them an overview and a way back to a named position.

records.title: The tasks a reader of a structure performs
records.statement: Shneiderman, The Eyes Have It, IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages 1996 (https://doi.org/10.1109/VL.1996.545307): overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand, then relate, history and extract - seven tasks, and a viewer that omits one of them leaves the reader without a move.

records.title: A notation is judged by its visual variables
records.statement: Moody, The Physics of Notations, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.2009.67): a visual notation is judged by perceptual discriminability, dual coding and one symbol per concept, so shape, outline and tone must carry a meaning together instead of colour carrying it alone.

records.title: Geometry is read more accurately than hue
records.statement: Cleveland and McGill, Graphical Perception, Journal of the American Statistical Association 1984 (https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1984.10478080): position and length are decoded more accurately than area or colour, so anything a reader must compare belongs in geometry and colour stays a label.

records.title: Layout says things the notation never states
records.statement: Petre, Why Looking Isn't Always Seeing, Communications of the ACM 1995 (https://doi.org/10.1145/203241.203251): arrangement carries meaning the notation never states and only a practised reader sees it, so a generated picture must not let accidental placement stand in for a stated fact.

records.title: Hierarchical layout is a solved, stated algorithm
records.statement: Sugiyama, Tagawa and Toda, Methods for Visual Understanding of Hierarchical System Structures, IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics 1981 (https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1981.4308636), shipped as the layered algorithm this library asks ELK for (https://eclipse.dev/elk/reference/algorithms/org-eclipse-elk-layered.html): layer assignment, crossing reduction and straightening make a dependency graph readable without anybody placing a box by hand.

records.title: Three response budgets a reader can feel
records.statement: Card, Robertson and Mackinlay, The Information Visualizer, CHI 1991 (https://doi.org/10.1145/108844.108874): 0.1 second reads as a direct response, 1 second keeps a train of thought unbroken and 10 seconds is the limit of held attention - the budgets any layout sharing the interface thread has to fit.

records.title: One architecture, several views
records.statement: Kruchten, The 4+1 View Model of Architecture, IEEE Software 1995 (https://doi.org/10.1109/52.469759): one architecture is described by several views written for different concerns, so several documents rendered from one snapshot answer more than a single diagram trying to answer everything.

records.title: A module hides a decision
records.statement: Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 1972 (https://doi.org/10.1145/361598.361623): a module exists to hide a decision behind its interface, which makes a layer table and a one-way import rule part of the description of the design rather than a lint preference.

records.title: A rejection names the rule it broke
records.statement: Meyer, Applying 'Design by Contract', IEEE Computer 1992 (https://doi.org/10.1109/2.161279): a component states its precondition, so a caller that violates one can be told which obligation it missed instead of receiving an anonymous failure.

records.title: Accessibility is a stated conformance list
records.statement: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), with the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/): keyboard operation, a cue that is not colour alone, contrast, reflow, a respected motion preference and an announced status change are numbered success criteria and named widget patterns, not matters of taste.

records.title: Status and errors in the reader’s language
records.statement: Nielsen, 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/): visibility of system status, user control, and error messages that state the problem in plain language and suggest a remedy.

records.title: A dated dialect and a graded change
records.statement: JSON Schema 2020-12 (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core) and Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html): the contract is declared in a dated dialect and every change to it is graded, so a consumer can tell an addition from a removal before upgrading.

records.title: A diagram is defined by its level and its audience
records.statement: Brown, the C4 model for visualising software architecture (https://c4model.com/): context, container, component and code are levels of one description with different audiences, which is what a zoom threshold has to correspond to if the map is to replace them.

records.title: No fact is carried by colour alone
records.rule: Every distinction the map or a generated diagram draws - zone, kind, interaction, selection, staleness - is carried by at least two of tone, shape, outline, line and text, and the text form alone is enough to read it.
when: A node, a relation or a state is drawn in the map or in a generated diagram.
exceptions: A purely decorative surface that states no model fact.

records.title: A second channel exists for every distinction
records.assertion: For each value of every drawn contract enum the appearance table names a non-colour channel as well as a tone, and the panel states the same value in words.

records.title: Ask for a layered graph rather than place boxes
records.choice: Compute geometry with the ELK layered algorithm - the Sugiyama pipeline - loaded on demand, and treat its output as the only source of position and size.
alternatives: Store coordinates in the snapshot and let an author place each box.
records.because: A dependency graph read top to bottom needs layer assignment and crossing reduction, both solved by a stated algorithm, and hand-placed coordinates would make arrangement a fact nobody validates.
consequences: Layout cost grows with the model, so it has to move off the interface thread to keep the response budget.
A reader cannot nudge a box; a bad reading is fixed by changing the model or the layout options.

records.title: Read a system nobody explained
records.actor: An owner new to the system
given: A validated snapshot of a system with more parts than fit on one screen is mounted.
steps: Read the overview and the stated level.
Search for a part by name.
Zoom it past its threshold until its children appear in place.
Follow one relation to a neighbour and read the closure of what a change to it reaches.
Copy the address and open it again in a new tab.
failures: A name that matches nothing states so instead of clearing the map.
An address naming an absent record is refused with a stated failure.

records.title: Read the map with a keyboard and a screen reader
records.actor: A reader using a keyboard, a screen reader and a reduced-motion setting
given: A validated snapshot is mounted in a browser with the reader’s own settings.
steps: Reach the map by tab and traverse it by arrow key.
Select a part and read the panel.
Change the level and hear what changed.
Enlarge the text until the page reflows to one column.
failures: A part reachable by pointer but not by key fails the run.

records.title: Install it and mount a first map
given: Only the published package and its generated documentation are available.
steps: Follow the shipped page to install the package.
Write a first snapshot from the starting template.
Mount the map in an application and feed it that snapshot.
Break the snapshot on purpose and read the failure.
Upgrade to the next version and read what the version promised.
failures: An input past the stated bounds is rejected by name, not by exhaustion.
A snapshot from a newer major contract is refused with the grade of the difference.

records.title: Confirm, withdraw and compare
given: A snapshot with recorded outcomes and bound parts is loaded.
steps: Run a check and store its output as evidence.
Change one definition and read what lost its basis and why.
Read the described part against the file it binds to.
Compare the snapshot with the previous release.
Export the result for a tool outside the library.
failures: An outcome with no recorded run is refused.
Moved bytes ask for a reading instead of staying confirmed.

records.title: Regenerate every document
given: A validated snapshot and the committed generated documents are present.
steps: Regenerate the landing page, the reference and every diagram.
Parse each diagram with the renderer that will draw it.
Compare the result with the committed files.
Confirm a record carrying markup is drawn as text.
failures: Any drift between the model and a committed document fails the run.

records.title: Levels a reader can name
records.change: Give the map named zoom levels that correspond to abstraction, expand a container with hysteresis at its threshold, and state which level is shown.

records.title: An overview and a way back
records.change: Add a constant overview of the whole snapshot beside the detail, and a return to the previous position, so zooming never loses the surrounding context.

records.title: The view lives in the address
records.change: Encode selection, zoom, level and filters in the address, restore them on load, and reject an address that names a record the snapshot does not hold.

records.title: Search that does not depend on the contract version
records.change: Search records by name, type and zone through the model layer for every contract version the library accepts, instead of matching one version in the header component.

records.title: Filter, then relate
records.change: Filter the map by zone, kind and interaction kind, and highlight the neighbours of a selected part so a relation can be followed without reading every box.

records.title: What a change reaches
records.change: Compute the upstream and downstream closure of a selected record in the model layer and draw it, so the map answers where an effect reaches.

records.title: A layer is a view, not a dimming
records.change: Make a chosen layer a real projection - the parts of that zone with their relations - rather than a translucency over everything else.

records.title: Never colour alone
records.change: Give every drawn contract enum value a non-colour channel in the appearance table, name the value in words in the panel, and fail the suite when a value has only a tone.

records.title: A legend that cannot drift
records.change: Render the legend for the map and the generated diagram from the appearance table, so a new enum value appears in it without anybody writing it down.

records.title: Layout leaves the interface thread
records.change: Run ELK in a worker, keep the last good geometry while a new one is computed, and cancel a superseded layout.

records.title: Mount what is visible
records.change: Mount only the parts inside or near the viewport and release the rest, so a hundreds-of-parts model does not keep every node alive.

records.title: Measure the budget, do not assert it
records.change: Add a harness that loads a generated model of the stated size and records first response, interactive and full-layout times against the stated parameters.

records.title: Every read can be abandoned
records.change: Thread an abort signal through load, parse and layout, and stop the work when the caller withdraws.

records.title: Limits with a name
records.change: State the accepted bounds - bytes, records, depth, relation count - and reject anything past them with a named failure rather than an exhausted tab.

records.title: The map under a keyboard
records.change: Make the map a single tab stop with arrow traversal, enter to select, escape to leave a container, and the same reach a pointer has.

records.title: Focus that can be seen
records.change: Give every interactive element a visible focus ring that survives a high-contrast theme, and add the landmarks and headings a reader jumps between.

records.title: Say what changed
records.change: Announce a loaded model, a selection, a level change and a failure through a live region, so a change the reader did not type is not silent.

records.title: The reader owns the surface
records.change: Honour reduced motion, forced colours, colour scheme and text zoom, and keep the map usable when the page reflows to one column.

records.title: An accessibility failure fails the build
records.change: Run an accessibility audit and a keyboard walk-through in the browser harness and fail on a violation instead of on a screenshot review.

records.title: One table of failures
records.change: Generate a table of every failure code with what it means and what to do, from the same module that raises them, and publish it in the shipped documentation.

records.title: A failure is a picture, not an empty frame
records.change: Show a rejected or unreachable model as a stated failure inside the mounted surface, with the code, the record and the remedy.

records.title: Start from the shipped page
records.change: Generate the install, mount and first-failure walk-through from the model, with the exact commands and the mounting snippet a consumer copies.

records.title: What a version promises
records.change: Write down which exports, contract fields and asset paths are public, what a minor and a major change may do to them, and check the package against that list.

records.title: Grade a contract change
records.change: Compare the shipped contract with the previous one, grade the difference as additive or breaking, and refuse a snapshot from a newer major with a named failure.

records.title: Shipped copies say they are copies
records.change: Rename the shipped model and copy assets so a consumer cannot mistake them for their own project file, and release the change as a break.

records.title: Terms and history in the package
records.change: Add the licence the package claims and generate the release history from the snapshot, so what changed between two versions is readable without Git.

records.title: Start from something valid
records.change: Add a command that writes a minimal valid snapshot with a scope, a source, a requirement and a criterion, so authoring never starts from an empty file.

records.title: A rejection that teaches
records.change: Point every validation failure at the record, the field and the value it read, and state the accepted shape beside it.

records.title: Compare two snapshots
records.change: Add a diff that reports added, removed and changed records between two snapshots, and what lost its basis as a result.

records.title: A claim has an age and an author
records.change: Record when a claim was written and by whom, and show a claim older than its stated life as ageing rather than as current.

records.title: A question is a first-class record
records.change: Surface every question-origin source as an open list in the map and the documentation, so an unanswered question is not filed as a fact.

records.title: Withdraw only what depended on it
records.change: Compute a per-definition basis so a changed definition withdraws its dependents instead of every basis in the snapshot.

records.title: What went stale, and why
records.change: Report every record that lost its basis with the definition that moved, as a reading list the author can work through.

records.title: Read the description against the file
records.change: Bind a described part to the region of code it claims, and when those bytes move, ask for a reading instead of accepting the digest as proof of meaning.

records.title: An outcome comes from a run
records.change: Run a check command, store its output as evidence with the contract it ran against, and refuse an outcome nobody ran.

records.title: A snapshot travels
records.change: Export a snapshot as the graph other tools read - DOT, mermaid and a flat record table - from the same projection the map draws.

records.title: The generated diagram is parsed, not eyeballed
records.change: Parse every generated diagram with the renderer that will draw it, in the browser harness, so a syntax error fails the build.

records.title: Model content stays inert
records.change: Prove that a record carrying markup, a link or a script is drawn as text in every surface and every generated document.

records.title: English, and all of it
records.change: Check that every string the interface can show exists in the shipped copy, in English, with both plural forms, and fail on a missing key.

records.title: Zooming, overview and address
records.method: Drive the mounted map in a browser: cross a threshold, read the stated level, return to the previous position, and restore a view from its address.

records.title: Finding and relating a part
records.method: Search a part by name in each accepted contract version, filter by zone, and read the closure of a selected record.

records.title: Keyboard, announcement and second channel
records.method: Audit the mounted surface for accessibility violations, walk it by keyboard only, and confirm every drawn enum value has a channel that is not a tone.

records.title: The stated budget on a stated model
records.method: Load a generated model of the stated size and record first response, interactive and full-layout times, and confirm a withdrawn read stops.

records.title: Every failure is named and explained
records.method: Feed each rejection path a bad input and confirm the code, the record it names and the remedy, in the API, the CLI and the mounted surface.

records.title: Generated documents agree with the model
records.method: Regenerate every document, parse the diagrams, confirm no drift against the committed files and that model content stays inert English text.

records.title: What the package promises
records.method: Resolve every published export and asset path from an installed package and compare the contract with the previous release for a graded difference.

records.title: Provenance, withdrawal and history
records.method: Change one definition and confirm that only its dependents lose their basis, that the diff reports it, and that an outcome without a recorded run is refused.
